newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to release Red Cross workers on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to release Red Cross workers on Friday.

text.p: A Sudanese pro-government group will release on Friday three workers of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) it captured three weeks ago when it seized their plane, the Sudanese news agency SUNA said on Thursday.
The Bahr al-Ghazal group, led by Kerubino Kwanyin Bol, had agreed after talks with ICRC representatives to release the plane's two pilots and a nurse.
Sudan on November 7 suspended all ICRC work, saying the plane was carrying arms and troops loyal to the rebel Sudan People Liberation Army (SPLA) headed by Colonel John Garang.
For 13 years, the SPLA has been fighting for the autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south from Sudan's Islamist dominated north.
The plane flew from northern Kenya to Wunruk in Sudan's Bahr el-Ghazal province
The three ICRC workers are from Canada, Kenya and Australia. Five Sudanese patients were also on the plane but it is not clear what happened to them.
SUNA said Bol and the ICRC agreed that "appropriate measures be taken to prevent a repetition of this kind of practise," but did not give details.
